For the cost of direct loans, loan guarantees, insurance, and tied-aid grants as authorized by section 10 of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945, as amended, $100,000,000, to remain available 
until September 30, 2009: Provided, That such costs, including the cost of modifying such loans, shall be as defined in section 502 of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974: Provided further, That such sums shall remain available until September 30, 2024, for the disbursement of direct loans, loan guarantees, insurance and tied-aid grants obligated in fiscal years 2006, 2007, 2008, and 2009: Provided further, That none of the funds appropriated by this Act or any prior Act appropriating funds for foreign operations, export financing, and related programs for tied-aid credits or grants may be used for any other purpose except through the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations: Provided further, That funds appropriated by this paragraph are made available notwithstanding section 2(b)(2) of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945, in connection with the purchase or lease of any product by any Eastern European country, any Baltic State or any agency or national thereof.

fable.w: This is an appropriations paragraph funding Export-Import Bank loans, guarantees, insurance and tied-aid grants. The tempting reading is that the "regular notification procedures" amount to a consultation process, but they run only to the congressional Committees on Appropriations, which are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, company, expert or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing, or granted a right to sue or object.
fable.s: may be used for any other purpose except through the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that restricts the use of funds. The only procedural requirement mentioned is 'regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations.' Since Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, notifying them does not constitute participation by outside parties. There is no mention of public comment, hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_block.s: none of the funds appropriated by this Act or any prior Act appropriating funds for foreign operations, export financing, and related programs for tied-aid credits or grants may be used for any other purpose except through the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations

opus.w: The only procedural step here is notifying the congressional Appropriations Committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so this is not participation. Everything else covers funding amounts, how long the funds stay available, and loan eligibility. No states, experts, members of the public or other outside parties are consulted, and no one gets a right to sue.
opus.s: may be used for any other purpose except through the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the "regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations" count as a formal consultation step before funds are used for another purpose. That fails the definition because the Appropriations Committees are part of Congress, which is inside the federal government. The rest of the section is funding terms. The mention of Eastern European countries concerns loan eligibility, not their involvement in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The notification is to Congress, which is inside the federal government. Notification to Congress is not participation. It looks like participation because it mentions "regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations."
qwen_chat.s: none of the funds appropriated by this Act or any prior Act appropriating funds for foreign operations, export financing, and related programs for tied-aid credits or grants may be used for any other purpose except through the regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "regular notification procedures of the Committees on Appropriations."
Resolution: The notification is to Congress, which is inside the federal government. Notification to Congress is not participation.
